correctness.rationale: Reaudited repairs/4/RESULT.md. The frozen last sentence of the Finding called K^(1/4) the fourth-power norm; the corrected text distinguishes the operator norm K^(1/4) from its fourth power K. For M fixed, Parseval and triangle inequality give the nonnegative autocorrelation majorant. Reflection-pair RMS preserves mass and increases each nonnegative lag correlation by Cauchy–Schwarz and AM–GM. On the reflected symmetric boundary α=0 or β=0 the effective three-term ratio is 1+8t−14t² for t in [0,1/2], giving 15/7; when γ=0 it is 1+(1+6t(1−t))/2 for t in [0,1], giving 9/4. Both are below even the flat five-mode trial 17/5. Thus compactness gives a positive symmetric maximizer. Saturation at lags four and two forces every original maximizing magnitude vector to be symmetric as well. Section 4 of python3 -B /workspace/review-evidence/rederive.py independently obtained F from the two-sum fibers and performed exact rational elimination in x². The x² stationary value is the stated rational function of y; after substitution the remaining derivative is the negative of the stated first quartic times a strictly positive rational factor. Descartes and the sign change give one positive root; compactness and the boundary bounds therefore yield the unique optimizing ratios. The exact expression for K and the rounded ordinates agree. Lag one forces constant phase increments once magnitudes are positive, and affine phases suffice in all lags. The nine differences are distinct for every N≥9. The frozen verify.py and VERIFICATION.md were inspected, not executed; the original calculations and independent symbolic checks support the polynomial identities, not by themselves global optimality.

value.rationale: The degree-four interval is a canonical finite Fourier/Nikolskii problem, not a searched selection of irregular parameters. The exact algebraic value distinguishes the nonflat maximizing polynomial from the flat Dirichlet trial and the boundary spectra, and gives every complex optimizer. For this natural fixed-degree question the interior two-parameter solve, explicit constant and equality classification are mathematically useful beyond the standard majorant and symmetry reductions.
